title: Mexican Government Seeks Free Admission to 53 Museums and Archaeological Sites Next Year
author: Dora Villanueva
content:
_This article by[Dora
Villanueva](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Dora%20Villanueva) originally
appeared in the [September 10, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/09/10/cultura/gobierno-
federal-busca-gratuidad-en-53-museos-y-zonas-arqueologicas-para-proximo-ano),
Mexico’s premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City.** The federal government is seeking to make admission to 53
sites —among them museums, monuments, and archaeological sites— **free** ,
given that the administrative and operating costs of charging for access to
them are **“disproportionate relative to the revenue”** obtained. As part of
the changes proposed to the Federal Rights Law for next year, Bonampak, in
Chiapas; La Venta, in Tabasco; and Tamtoc, in San Luis Potosí, are among the
sites that, under the administration of the National Institute of Anthropology
and History (INAH), will offer free admission.

“This measure will make it possible to simplify administrative operations at
those sites where the charging scheme is inefficient and, at the same time,
**favor the public’s access to these cultural assets and promote Mexico’s
cultural heritage** ,” the Presidency explained in next year’s Federal Rights
Law initiative.

The free admission proposed by the Presidency would apply to the Chapel of
Tepozcolula and the Casa del Deán; to the former convents of San Francisco
Tecamachalco, Santa María Magdalena Cuitzeo, Oxtotipac, San Andrés Epazoyucan,
and San Francisco Huaquechula; as well as to the historic monument Chapel of
Tlalmanalco. Also to the Guillermo Spratling, Huastec Culture, Estampa, and
Valle de Tehuacán museums, and the Tuxteco museum; to the archaeological
museums of Ciudad Guzmán, Camino Real Hecelchakán, and Soconusco; to the
historical museum of eastern Morelos, the Baluarte de Santiago, and the
Regional Museum of La Laguna; as well as to the Juan Gamboa Guzmán Pinacoteca,
located in Mérida, Yucatán.

In addition to Bonampak and Tamtoc, the free archaeological sites would be
Boca de Potrerillos, Cuyuxquihui, Izapa, Pomoná, Tehuacalco, La Ferrería, and
Lagartero, according to the Federal Rights Law initiative.

And, among the archaeological zones, in addition to La Venta and its museum,
free admission is proposed for Calixtlahuaca, Chalchihuites, Coatetelco (with
museum), Chacmultún, Cuajilote, Dainzú, Hochob, Ihuatzio, Malpasito,
Toluquilla, Tres Zapotes (with museum), El Chanal, Huandacareo La Nopalera, La
Campana, Lambityeco, Las Labradas, Las Pilas, Los Melones, San Felipe Los
Alzati, Santa Cecilia Acatitlán (with museum), Tizatlán (with museum), Tres
Cerritos, Vega de La Peña, and Santa Rosa Xtampak.

Although these 53 sites under INAH’s management will be free, **payment to
access another 122 remains** in the proposal the Presidency sent to Congress.
